clue.text: A short time with saint and prophet

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: A brief visit to a holy figure and a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Calculus marker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: calculus is the hard deposit on teeth
second meaning: a commemorative tablet marking where someone lived

explanation.walkthrough: Calculus looks like the branch of mathematics, but here it is the dentist's word for tartar.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental tartar is also called calculus, and a wall tablet such as a blue plaque marks a historic site.

clue.text: Support current recovery

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
wind is a current of air

explanation.surface: Backing an electric flow to get it working again.
explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is a renewed burst of energy after tiredness, a recovery of stamina.

clue.text: Hat: article wrapped by parents

indicators.note: something wrapped by another thing sits inside it, so the article goes within the parents

parts.note: pa and ma are the two parents
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A hat with a grammatical word enclosed by mother and father.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight brimmed straw hat, originally made in Ecuador.

clue.text: Champions raising funds to acquire baseball player

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it, so champions means backs

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word upwards, so funds is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pot is a fund of money, as in the kitty or jackpot

explanation.surface: Winners putting up money to sign a new player for their team.
explanation.walkthrough: Champions means backs (supports). Funds gives POT, a pool of money, and 'raising' turns it upward in this down clue to TOP; the plural is loose, since POTS would leave a spare S.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the backstop is the catcher, the player stationed behind home plate.

clue.text: Callus in ear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small painful callus on the foot
second meaning: an ear of ..., the cereal crop

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests hard skin inside an ear; the two words are separate meanings joined by in.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn is a patch of hardened skin on a toe, and an ear is the seed head of a cereal crop.

clue.text: Sweet I stuff into tailored suit

indicators.note: into places the stuffing inside the other letters
a tailored suit is cut and reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Someone cramming a dessert into the pockets of a bespoke suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuff looks like a noun (I stuff the pudding) but is the verb ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge layered with mascarpone cream.

clue.text: Wanderers out to catch leader in Everton, one delivering report

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the anagram holds the extra letter
out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the leader in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A football match report: Wanderers playing away at Everton.
explanation.walkthrough: Wanderers and Everton look like football clubs (Bolton Wanderers, Everton). 'out' rearranges WANDERERS, and 'to catch' puts E, the leader in Everton, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreader is the presenter who reads out the news on radio or television.

clue.text: Author left in big hole

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the hole

parts.note: a mine is a large hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A writer abandoned in a deep pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne was the English writer who created Winnie-the-Pooh.

clue.text: Compare flavour of numerous liqueurs, keeping a record

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the flavour surrounds the other letters

parts.note: anise is the aniseed flavour of pastis, ouzo, sambuca and similar liqueurs
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A taster comparing liqueurs while keeping notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To analogise is to draw an analogy, likening one thing with another.

clue.text: Tree ring almost covered by water

indicators.note: something covered by another thing lies inside it

parts.note: the sea is a body of water

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: a quoit is a ring thrown in the game of quoits

explanation.surface: A tree with a ring nearly submerged in water.
explanation.walkthrough: A quoit is the ring tossed over a peg in the game of quoits.
explanation.definitionFit: The sequoia is the giant redwood of California, among the largest trees on earth.

clue.text: Important answer inspiring North African people

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the outer letters take in the letter for north

parts.note: key means important, as in a key figure

explanation.surface: A significant reply that motivates people from northern Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenyans are the people of Kenya, in East Africa.

clue.text: Belief, first of all, can really enhance every day

indicators.note: first of all takes the first letter of every one of the following words

explanation.surface: An upbeat claim that faith can improve each day.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a system of religious faith or a set of guiding principles.

clue.text: In retreat, notice US train line clearer?

indicators.note: In at the front says the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: to cower is to shrink back or retreat in fear
to catch is to notice, as in catching sight of something

explanation.surface: Spotting an American railway device while pulling back.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowcatcher is the angled frame on the front of an American locomotive that pushes obstacles off the track.

clue.text: Clear his ear out when runny

indicators.note: something runny has lost its shape and flows, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to clean out someone's ear when it is weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise something is to clear it, giving official permission to go ahead.

clue.text: First gorilla in new sanctuary, finally

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The first gorilla to arrive at a new animal sanctuary at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First gorilla' looks like a phrase, but First is the definition. 'new' rearranges GORILLA and IN, then 'finally' adds Y from sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally means at first, in the beginning, before later changes.

clue.text: Plug in hole initially, I saw off bit of gravy — with this?

definitions.text: Plug in hole initially, I saw off bit of gravy — with this?

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so these letters are rearranged
initially takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: gravy is slang for money, and a quid (British slang for one pound) is a bit of it

explanation.surface: Washing up: put the plug in, then scrub off the dried gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes doing the dishes, and the question asks what you use. 'off' rearranges PLUG, IN, H (the first of hole) and I SAW into WASHINGUPLI; QUID, a pound in British slang, completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing-up liquid is the British term for dishwashing detergent, squirted into a sink of hot water to clean greasy plates.

clue.text: As medicine man has turned crazy

indicators.note: turned means reworked, so these three letters are rearranged

parts.note: manic means wildly excited or crazy

explanation.surface: A medicine man who has gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer or medicine man, so shamanic describes acting in that role.

clue.text: Something to play, well after drinks

indicators.note: after says the exclamation comes behind the drinks

parts.note: gin and rum are two drinks
my! and well! are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Something to play when you are well after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin rummy is a two-player card game, a version of rummy.

clue.text: After party, one in commercial left

indicators.note: in puts the party and one inside the commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: After says one comes behind the party

parts.note: a band is a group or party of people
one taken as a word

explanation.surface: Someone who quit after a party, appearing in an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means deserted, the past tense of leaving something behind.

clue.text: Lovely to polish off forged shield

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Buffing up a counterfeit shield would be pleasant work.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish off looks like cleaning the shield, but it means eat up: the definition is the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Delish is informal for delicious, so food that is delish is lovely to eat up.

clue.text: First person in Germany with golden, sacred flower?

parts.note: ich is German for I, the first person pronoun
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: The writer in Germany with a golden, holy bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower is not a bloom but something that flows: ichor flows in the veins of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor is the fluid running through the gods' veins, a divine liquid that flows.

clue.text: Direct, perfect way

parts.note: to hone a skill is to perfect it
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A straightforward and flawless route.
explanation.definitionFit: An honest, direct person speaks plainly and frankly without deceit.

clue.text: Fortified building used primarily by Earl Grey, twice?

parts.note: Earl Grey is a tea, given twice as cha (slang for tea) and tea

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A castle where Earl Grey is mostly drunk, double strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Earl Grey looks like an aristocrat, but it is the bergamot-flavoured tea; cha is an old British slang word for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or large country house, originally a fortified residence.

clue.text: Some knighted, English PM

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of a British prime minister who was given a knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Anthony Eden was British Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957, and was indeed knighted.

clue.text: Experienced runner regularly seen in front

indicators.note: seen in says the picked letters appear inside the other word

parts.note: to be in the lead is to be in front

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the odd ones

explanation.surface: A seasoned athlete who is often seen at the head of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned can mean gained by experience or study, as in a learned response or learned behaviour.

clue.text: Misery in humour uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting raises the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a humour is a mood, as in being in good humour

explanation.surface: Finding gloom in cheerful comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom suggests a grim fate or a sense of despair and wretchedness.

clue.text: Ground deep, rim is layer on surface

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a crater: a deep hole in the ground with a rim.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of the skin, lying on the body's surface.

clue.text: Rope, as secured by London players

indicators.note: secured by means held inside, so the word as sits within the orchestra

parts.note: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A rope used to tie up some London musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope used by cowboys for catching cattle.
